summary:
⚠️ Risk Score: MEDIUM (45/100)

1 Critical · 1 High · 1 Medium

Review completed with 3 findings across 2 agents (1 critical, 1 high, 1 medium).

⚠️ 2 critical/high severity issues require immediate attention:
  - [CRITICAL] Regression of XSS vulnerability due to removed URLField scheme validation (LogicAgent)
  - [HIGH] Removal of regression test for unsafe URL scheme handling (LogicAgent)
🛡️ 1 severity cap(s) applied by deterministic post-processing:
  - capped CRITICAL->MEDIUM (hedged title): Missing URL scheme sanitization leading to potential XSS

findings.title: Regression of XSS vulnerability due to removed URLField scheme validation
findings.description: Removing the `ValidationError` import is safe in the current diff because its sole usage (in the `URLField` validation block) is also deleted. No remaining references to `ValidationError` or `URLValidator` exist in the modified scope, so no `NameError` will occur at runtime. However, the broader impact of removing this security mitigation is severe: the admin will now render any stored `URLField` value as a clickable HTML link without validating its scheme. If a value with a dangerous scheme (e.g., `javascript:` or `data:`) is stored, it will be rendered as an executable link in the admin changelist and read-only views, re-introducing the XSS vulnerability described in the reverted CVE-2026-15920 release notes. The diff proves this regression path because `display_for_field` now unconditionally calls `format_html('{}', value, value)` for `URLField` instances where `value` is truthy, bypassing any scheme check. This is a critical logic and security regression in production if unsanitized user-controlled data can reach `URLField` values.
findings.suggestion: Restore the `ValidationError` and `URLValidator` imports, and reinstate the `try/except` validation block that checks `URLValidator()(value)` before rendering the link. Fallback to `display_for_value(value, empty_value_display)` on `ValidationError` to ensure unsafe schemes are displayed as plain text.

findings.title: Missing URL scheme sanitization leading to potential XSS
findings.description: The validation logic that used `URLValidator()(value)` to check for safe schemes is removed. `URLValidator` by default rejects `javascript:` and `data:` schemes, but the original code used it specifically to prevent XSS. By removing this check, the code now directly interpolates `value` into an `href` attribute without sanitization. While `format_html` escapes the value to prevent HTML injection into the tag structure, it does not prevent the browser from executing `javascript:` protocols in an `href` attribute if the value is not escaped from the perspective of URL scheme safety. This is the core mechanism of the XSS regression.
findings.suggestion: Re-add the `URLValidator` check. If `URLValidator` is deemed too strict or not covering all unsafe schemes, implement a dedicated scheme whitelist (e.g., `http`, `https`, `ftp`, `mailto`) and render as plain text if the scheme is not in the whitelist.

findings.title: Removal of regression test for unsafe URL scheme handling
findings.description: The test `test_url_display_for_field_invalid_url` is removed entirely. This test specifically asserted that dangerous URL schemes (`javascript:`, `data:`) would be rendered as plain text without an `<a>` tag. Deleting this test removes the regression safety net for the security fix being reverted. Combined with the removal of the production validation code, there is now no automated check ensuring that unsafe `URLField` values are not rendered as executable links. This is a HIGH severity issue from a quality assurance and security posture standpoint, as the codebase no longer verifies its own safety against XSS vectors in the admin.
findings.suggestion: Restore the `test_url_display_for_field_invalid_url` test to ensure that unsafe schemes continue to be rejected or rendered as plain text, providing regression coverage for the security fix.
